observations: reserve copies supplied allocation paths, preventing caller mutation after commitment
failed reservations leave graph unchanged including sequence, loan records and locks
default subtracts precisely still-reserved origin stake and releases same edge/origin locks
partial repayment greedily releases exactly repaid integer principal, preserves remainder
already defaulted borrower address cannot borrow again; identity/Sybil aliases remain out of scope
wildcard root consent is an explicit broad delegation policy up to four edges, not endpoint-specific approval
Strict positive integer checks reject float/bool stakes, edge limits, loan quantities, repayments and withdrawals without mutation
RLock serializes mutating methods; actual four-thread simultaneous request test admits exactly three 300000 loans against1000000 stake
allocate computes candidate allocations on copied origin/edge residual capacities and atomically commits via serialized reserve
Allocator depth cap is four edges, root consent checked, route uses no officer score or manual per-borrower grant
limitations: No token movement, deployed EVM execution, interest/default timing, wallet signature authorization, identity uniqueness, customer income provenance or collateral provenance enforcement
Public mutable graph state trusted to harness, not adversarial process isolation
Successful accounting tests demonstrate a proposed reference model, not deployed transitivity support or mainnet readiness
In-process reservation atomicity is provided by RLock; no durable EVM/distributed transaction or atomic graph-plus-cash settlement implemented.
Greedy routing can reject a feasible allocation: no residual reverse-edge max-flow search, optimality, fairness or calibrated creditworthiness claim.
Dense graphs need cumulative search work/memory budget; recommended 1000 queue/candidate visits shared across roots and all split allocations.
